pages.title: Context diagram
pages.subtitle: PK Document Tracking System - implemented data exchanges
notes: Actors are functional responsibilities and may be performed by the same account. Role permissions determine available actions; an approver is selected by the published workflow.
Only information about physical document dispatch and receipt crosses the software boundary. The paper itself is not a software data flow.
All account holders authenticate as registered users. No email, SMS or external document cloud is evidenced in the operational code.
Level 0 is presented as six coordinated subsystem sheets (2-7) using the same process and store identifiers. Cross-sheet ports identify shared audit capture.

notes: Request types: softcopy_create, softcopy_revise, softcopy_cancel, hardcopy_create, hardcopy_update, transfer, disposal, access and assignment. Draft deletion is limited to the owner's cancelled, unsubmitted request.

Submission pins a published workflow graph/version and resolves user, role, requester or requester_leader assignments. Approve/reject/return updates the active step and history; only final approval applies the domain proposal atomically.

An approved transfer creates for_transfer data. Only the transfer requester dispatches it; only the named recipient accepts it. Acceptance updates holder/location, revokes the previous holder's personal grant and completes the request.

notes: Audit data is stored as private daily JSON arrays, not an operational SQL audit table. Audit listing filters these files. Backup/restore permissions are separately checked.

A backup contains a SQL dump plus application/private files, excluding sessions/cache and backup recursion. Its ZIP entries are AES-256 encrypted and the manifest is signed; imported archives are verified.

Web restore reapplies the database and private working data after a pre-restore recovery snapshot. Application-code recovery is offline. Restore maintenance blocks ordinary requests; retention maintains managed archives and daily audit/application logs.

pages.title: Logical store catalog and scope
pages.subtitle: Physical implementation mapping for D1-D4; boxes define logical stores used on sheets 2-7.
notes: Source-derived design snapshot of the Desktop checkout. Seed roles include Administrator, Document Control Officer, Plant Manager, Internal Auditor and Staff; permissions and workflow assignments remain configurable.

No operational SQL table for audit is used. The notifications table exists in the schema, but current inbox/pending logic reads requests + workflow_steps + task_notification_receipts; notifications appears only in draft cleanup.
revision_artifacts, settings and schema_migrations exist in the SQL snapshot; no active application read/write was found, so they are schema context rather than depicted business-flow stores.
Office/WPS review uses optional local protocol handlers and a signed content URL. CDN assets/ngrok tooling are deployment/client dependencies, not document-approval data services.

Backups contain a SQL dump plus application/private files, excluding transient sessions/cache and backup recursion. Web restore reapplies the database and private working data; application-code recovery is offline.

nodes.label:
D1  Identity and configuration
SQL: users, roles, user_roles, role_permissions, permissions,
login_attempts; areas, specifics, assets, locations, categories;
workflows, workflow_versions
Private session files: storage/sessions

D2  Document, file and custody records
SQL: hardcopy_documents, softcopy_documents, softcopy_revisions,
status_history, disposals, files, assignments, access_grants, transfers
Controlled file bytes: storage/documents/<random storage_name>
Softcopy assignments use assignments; hardcopy assignments update holder_id.

D3  Request and approval runtime
SQL: requests, workflow_steps, workflow_history, task_notification_receipts
Stored data: proposal payload, pinned workflow/version, active assignments,
decision history and per-user task occurrence receipts

D4  Audit and recovery files
Daily audit JSON arrays: storage/audit/YYYY-MM-DD.json
Encrypted AES-256 ZIP archives: storage/backups (or configured safe backup path)
Backups carry a signed manifest, SQL snapshot and application/private files.
Retention maintains managed backups, daily audit and application logs.
